The fourth and final season of the reimagined science fiction television series ''[[Battlestar Galactica (2004 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]'' premiered on the [[Syfy|Sci-Fi Channel]] in the United States on April 4, 2008, and concluded on March 20, 2009. Similar to the second season, it was [[split television season|split]] into two parts, each containing 10 episodes. "Season 4.0" aired from April to June 2008 and "Season 4.5" aired from January to March 2009. The fourth season contained 20 episodes, plus the television film ''[[Battlestar Galactica: Razor|Razor]]''.

* [[Jamie Bamber]] as [[Lee Adama|Lee "Apollo" Adama]]

* [[Tricia Helfer]] as [[Number Six (Battlestar Galactica)|Number Six]]
* [[Grace Park (actress)|Grace Park]] as [[Number Eight (Battlestar Galactica)|Sharon "Boomer" Valerii/Sharon "Athena" Agathon]] (Number Eight)

These actors are credited ''after'' the opening sequence:
* [[Michael Hogan (Canadian actor)|Michael Hogan]] as [[Saul Tigh]]

* [[Tahmoh Penikett]] as [[Karl Agathon|Karl "Helo" Agathon]]

* [[Alessandro Juliani]] as [[Felix Gaeta]]

}}</onlyinclude>

==Production==
During the hiatus after season 3, the writers had a retreat in [[Lake Tahoe]] where they planned much of the story arc for the fourth season, mainly mapping out the storylines of the first 10 episodes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://featuresblogs.chicagotribune.com/entertainment_tv/2009/01/final-fifth-cylon-ellen-tigh-battlestar-galactica-dualla-dee-.html|title='Battlestar Galactica's' Ron Moore addresses the shocking developments of 'Sometimes a Great Notion'|work=Chicago Tribune|first=Maureen|last=Ryan|date=January 17, 2009|access-date=July 13, 2011|archive-date=March 10, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310234009/http://featuresblogs.chicagotribune.com/entertainment_tv/2009/01/final-fifth-cylon-ellen-tigh-battlestar-galactica-dualla-dee-.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In June 2007, the Sci-Fi Channel confirmed the fourth season would be its final season, with an order of 22 episodes,<ref name="chicago tribune">{{cite web|url=http://featuresblogs.chicagotribune.com/entertainment_tv/2007/06/battlestar_gala.html|title='Battlestar Galactica' set to say goodbye after Season 4|work=Chicago Tribune|first=Maureen|last=Ryan|date=June 1, 2007|access-date=July 13, 2011|archive-date=December 20, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111220110941/http://featuresblogs.chicagotribune.com/entertainment_tv/2007/06/battlestar_gala.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> an increase from 13 as originally announced.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2007/03/22/sci-fi-extends-galactica-season-4-episode-order-to-22-23955/20070322scifi04/|title=Sci Fi Extends 'Galactica' Season 4 Episode Order to 22|publisher=Sci Fi|date=March 22, 2007|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> Production of the final season began in May 2007.<ref name="chicago tribune"/> A special TV movie, titled ''[[Battlestar Galactica: Razor]]'', aired on November 24, 2007. The regular season began airing on April 4, 2008.

Only the first 12 episodes of season four (including ''Razor'', which is technically the first two episodes of the 22 ordered for season 4<ref name="chicago tribune"/>) were filmed before the [[2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike]] halted production of all scripted TV shows.<ref>{{cite web |last=Goldman |first=Eric |date=February 11, 2008 |title=Battlestar Galactica's Post-Strike Battle Plan |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2008/02/11/battlestar-galacticas-post-strike-battle-plan |access-date= |publisher=IGN}}</ref> After the strike ended, the final 10 episodes began airing on January 16, 2009.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2008/10/16/battlestar-galactica-returns-on-sci-fi-journeys-end-draws-near-for-acclaimed-series-29200/20081016scifi01/|title=Battlestar Galactica Returns on Sci Fi/Journey's End Draws Near for Acclaimed Series|publisher=Sci Fi|date=October 16, 2008|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref>

==Reception==
The season received universal acclaim from critics, scoring 85 out of 100 based on 16 reviews from [[Metacritic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metacritic.com/tv/battlestar-galactica-2003/season-4|title=Battlestar Galactica (2003): Season 4|website=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> On [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the season has an approval rating of 92% with an average score of 8.1 out of 10 based on 38 reviews. The website's critical consensus reads, "''Battlestar Galactica''{{'}}s final season proves a satisfying conclusion to TV's best science fiction offering."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/battlestar-galactica/s04 |title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 4 |website=Rotten Tomatoes |accessdate=November 12, 2021}}</ref> The series also placed on numerous critics top ten lists of both 2008 and 2009 by publications such as the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'', ''[[The Star-Ledger]]'', ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' and ''[[TV Guide]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2008/|title=Best TV Shows of 2008|publisher=Metacritic|access-date=July 13, 2011|archive-date=June 16, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616142923/http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2008/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2009/|title=Best TV Shows of 2009|publisher=Metacritic|access-date=July 13, 2011|archive-date=June 25, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110625093707/http://apps.metacritic.com/tv/bests/2009/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The fourth season received a total of eleven [[Emmy Award]] nominations. "Season 4.0" received six nominations at the [[60th Primetime Emmy Awards]], for Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series ([[Michael Angeli]] for "Six of One"), Outstanding Cinematography for a One-Hour Series (Stephen McNutt for ''Razor''), Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Drama Series ("He That Believeth in Me"), and Outstanding Sound Mixing for a Comedy or Drama Series (One-Hour) (''Razor'');<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2008/07/17/sci-fi-channel-scores-its-most-ever-emmy-nominations-including-best-miniseries-for-tin-man-28203/20080717scifi01/|title=Sci Fi Channel Scores Its Most Ever Emmy Nominations Including Best Miniseries for 'Tin Man'|publisher=Sci Fi|date=July 17, 2008|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> and won for Outstanding Special Visual Effects for a Series ("He That Believeth in Me") and Outstanding Special Class – Short-Format Live-Action Entertainment Programs (''Razor Flashbacks'').<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2008/09/13/2008-creative-arts-emmy-awards-winners-28786/20080913atas01/|title=2008 Creative Arts Emmy Awards Winners|publisher=The Academy of Television Arts & Sciences|date=September 13, 2008|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> "Season 4.5" received five nominations at the [[61st Primetime Emmy Awards]], with the episode "Daybreak, Part 2" receiving all the series' nominations, for Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series ([[Michael Rymer]]), Outstanding Single Camera Picture Editing for a Drama Series, Outstanding Sound Mixing for a Comedy or Drama Series (One Hour), and Outstanding Special Visual Effects for a Series;<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2009/07/16/the-61st-primetime-emmy-awards-and-2009-creative-arts-emmy-awards-nominees-are-32009/20090716atas01/|title=The 61st Primetime Emmy(R) Awards and 2009 Creative Arts Emmy(R) Awards Nominees Are...|publisher=The Academy of Television Arts & Sciences|date=July 16, 2009|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> and won for Outstanding Sound Editing for a Series.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2009/09/20/nbc-wins-16-total-emmys-at-61st-annual-primetime-emmy-awards-32762/20090920nbc01/|title=NBC Wins 16 Total Emmys at 61st Annual Primetime Emmy Awards|publisher=NBC|date=September 20, 2009|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref>

For the 10 regular episodes, ''Battlestar Galactica'' averaged a 1.7 [[Nielsen ratings|Nielsen]] household rating and 2.2 million total viewers. This represented an increase of 13% in household rating and 11% in total viewers.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/ratings/2008/06/16/battlestar-galacticas-mid-season-finale-leads-sci-fi-to-double-digit-ratings-gains--27879/20080616scifi02/|title=Battlestar Galactica's Mid-Season Finale Leads Sci Fi to Double-Digit Ratings Gains|publisher=Sci Fi|date=June 16, 2008|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> The series finale received 2.4 million viewers and became the most-watched episode of the series in over three years.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/ratings/2009/03/24/battlestar-galactica-finale-blasts-away-the-competition-30760/20090324scifi01/|title=Battlestar Galactica Finale Blasts Away the Competition|publisher=Sci Fi|date=March 24, 2009|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref>

==Home video releases==
Similar to the second season, the fourth season was split into two parts, as well the DVD and Blu-ray sets. Season 4.0 was released on DVD in region 1 on January 6, 2009,<ref name="season 4.0">{{cite web|url=http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/35930/battlestar-galactica-season-40/|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season 4.0|first=Todd|last=Douglass Jr.|date=January 10, 2009|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> in region 2 (although simply titled "Season 4") on October 6, 2008<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B001CD9K9G/|title=Battlestar Galactica: Season 4|date=October 6, 2008 |publisher=Amazon.co.uk|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> and in region 4 (titled "Season 4: Part 1") on December 3, 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/802772|title=Battlestar Galactica (2004) - Season 4: Part 1|publisher=EzyDVD|access-date=July 13, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100420072612/http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/802772|archive-date=April 20, 2010}}</ref> Season 4.5 was released on DVD in region 1 on July 28, 2009,<ref name="season 4.5">{{cite web|url=http://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/38240/battlestar-galactica-season-45/|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season 4.5|first=Elizabeth|last=Neilson|date=August 19, 2009|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> in region 2 (titled "The Final Season") on June 1, 2009<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B001Q3KA64/|title=Battlestar Galactica - The Final Season|date=June 2009 |publisher=Amazon.co.uk|access-date=July 13, 2011}}</ref> and in region 4 (titled "Season 4: Part 2 – The Final Chapter") on July 28, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/805631|title=Battlestar Galactica (2004) - Season 4: Part 2 - The Final Chapter|publisher=EzyDVD|access-date=July 13, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100305113824/http://www.ezydvd.com.au/item.zml/805631|archive-date=March 5, 2010}}</ref> The complete fourth season was released on [[Blu-ray Disc]] in region 1 on January 4, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/releases/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-4-Blu-ray/10519|title=Battlestar Galactica - Season 4|publisher=TVShowsOnDVD|access-date=July 13, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101017000910/http://www.tvshowsondvd.com/releases/Battlestar-Galactica-Season-4-Blu-ray/10519|archive-date=October 17, 2010}}</ref>

The Season 4.0 DVD set includes the first 10 episodes of season four and the television film ''Razor''. The ''Razor'' disc includes the broadcast version as well as the unrated extended version. Executive producer [[Ronald D. Moore]] and writer [[Michael Taylor (screenwriter)|Michael Taylor]] provide commentary for the extended version. Also included on the ''Razor'' disc are deleted scenes, two featurettes—"The Look of ''Battlestar Galactica''" and "My Favorite Episode So Far", as well as a sneak peek at season 4. For the other discs, special features include creator Ronald D. Moore's podcast commentaries on 7 of the 10 episodes; podcasts for "Guess What's Coming to Dinner?" and "Sine Qua Non" were not recorded, while a podcast for "Faith" was recorded and is available on the official website but is not included on the sets due to the recording quality. With that, new commentaries were recorded for the DVD. Moore, along with writers [[Bradley Thompson]] and [[David Weddle]] provide commentary for "Faith"; Moore and writer [[Michael Angeli]] provide commentary for "Guess What's Coming to Dinner?"; and Moore and writer Michael Taylor prove commentary for "Sine Qua Non". Moore is joined by writer [[Jane Espenson]], editor Michael O'Halloran and supervising editor Andrew Seklir on his podcast commentary for "The Hub"; and is joined by writers Bradley Thompson and David Weddle, and editor Julius Ramsay on his podcast commentary for "Revelations". Also included are deleted scenes for every episode, ten [[David Eick]] videoblogs, three featurettes—"The Journey", "Cylons: The Twelve", and "The Music of ''Battlestar Galactica''", as well as a sneak peek of season 4.5 and a trailer for ''[[Caprica (TV series)|Caprica]]''.<ref name="season 4.0"/>

The Season 4.5 DVD set includes the last 10 episodes of season four. Special features include creator Ronald D. Moore's podcast commentaries on all 10 episodes. There are also three unaired extended episodes, for "A Disquiet Follows My Soul", "Islanded in a Stream of Stars", and "Daybreak". The extended episodes feature commentary tracks; writer and director Ronald D. Moore on "A Disquiet Follows My Soul"; series star and episode director [[Edward James Olmos]] on "Islanded in a Stream of Stars"; and executive producers Ronald D. Moore and David Eick and director [[Michael Rymer]] on "Daybreak". Also included are deleted scenes for various episodes, 11 David Eick videoblogs, and five featurettes—"Evolution of a Cue", "And They Have a Plan", "The Journey Ends: The Arrival", "What the Frak is Going on With ''Battlestar Galactica''?", and "A Look Back".<ref name="season 4.5"/>
